tldr: Headlines across all 14 buckets converge on a single verdict bulletin: Duane 'Keffe D' Davis found guilty of murdering Tupac Shakur, closing a nearly 30-year cold case. Indian outlets alone break from the uniform verdict register by foregrounding the case's conspiracy theories and the unanswered question of who actually pulled the trigger.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Both Hindustan Times headlines foreground mystery and doubt rather than the verdict itself — 'bizarre conspiracy theories', 'Who really shot Tupac Shakur?' — making india the only bucket whose homepage framing foregrounds unresolved cultural mythology over the court's resolution.

One of two BBC headlines is experiential rather than informational ('What it was like inside court') — the only outlet in the corpus to lead with an eyewitness/narrative frame at headline level, suppressing the verdict itself in favour of atmospheric courtroom reporting.

bottom_line: The headline layer is a near-uniform verdict bulletin across all 14 buckets; the only meaningful divergence is Hindustan Times, which substitutes conspiracy-theory mythology and open questions for the settled-fact register used by every other outlet.
